title: Greeter survives a grace-time unlock; every later lock starts no greeter ("QProcess::start: Process is already running") and leaves a black screen with only a cursor
line: Locking the screen again after an unlock in grace time now always shows the lock screen, even if the old lock screen process got stuck.
explanation: An unlock within the grace time unlocks at once and only sends SIGTERM to the greeter. If that greeter doesn't exit (on the reporter's NVIDIA machine it ignored it), KSldApp keeps it in m_lockProcess, and the next lock calls QProcess::start() on a process that is still running, which only warns "Process is already running". The session is then locked with no greeter: a black screen with no password field. The change makes startLockProcess() SIGKILL a still-running old greeter and wait for it, with its exit treated like a grace-time kill (no crash counter), before starting the new one.

commits.message:
ksldapp: Kill a leftover greeter before starting a new one

An unlock in grace time only sends SIGTERM to the greeter. If it doesn't
exit, the next lock can't start a new greeter and the session stays
locked on a black screen with no password field, so kill the old one.

BUG: 528681

patches.diff:
From 88bdc02bde46e55109fa7573e5e41398dc2baf5c Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: =?UTF-8?q?Niccol=C3=B2=20Venerandi?= <niccolo@venerandi.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 17:12:02 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] ksldapp: Kill a leftover greeter before starting a new one

An unlock in grace time only sends SIGTERM to the greeter. If it doesn't
exit, the next lock can't start a new greeter and the session stays
locked on a black screen with no password field, so kill the old one.

BUG: 528681
---
 ksldapp.cpp | 9 +++++++++
 1 file changed, 9 insertions(+)

diff --git a/ksldapp.cpp b/ksldapp.cpp
index 2e83b2ac..bba405bf 100644
--- a/ksldapp.cpp
+++ b/ksldapp.cpp
@@ -382,6 +382,15 @@ void KSldApp::startLockProcess(EstablishLock establishLock)
 {
     qCDebug(KSCREENLOCKER) << "Starting lock process with establishLock:" << establishLockToString(establishLock);
 
+    if (m_lockProcess->state() != QProcess::NotRunning) {
+        // The previous greeter has not exited yet, e.g. it ignored the SIGTERM sent on an unlock in grace time.
+        // QProcess cannot start a new one while it runs, which would leave the session locked without a greeter.
+        qCWarning(KSCREENLOCKER) << "Previous greeter process is still running, killing it";
+        s_graceTimeKill = true; // makes the finished handler ignore its exit
+        m_lockProcess->kill();
+        m_lockProcess->waitForFinished();
+    }
+
     Q_EMIT aboutToStartGreeter();
 
     QProcessEnvironment env = m_greeterEnv;
-- 
2.53.0

media.caption: Master: greeter stalled during a grace unlock, then Lock: session locked, no greeter, black screen (journal: "QProcess::start: Process is already running")
With the fix, same steps: the stuck greeter is killed and a new lock screen with password field appears

review.text: Killing a leftover greeter before starting a new one does fix the black-screen lock, and the SIGSTOP repro shows it. But ksldapp runs inside kwin_wayland, and the unbounded waitForFinished() (default 30 s) blocks the compositor if the old greeter is slow to die, e.g. stuck in D state. The cleaner fix is at the point where the grace unlock sends SIGTERM, so a stuck greeter never lingers.
changes: In the grace-time unlock path, escalate to SIGKILL with a short timer if the greeter has not exited after SIGTERM
In startLockProcess, don't block the compositor: either use a short bounded waitForFinished (e.g. 500 ms) or start the new greeter from the old process's finished signal
